subject: Next steps and procurement ask — on-prem / VPC constraints for MedAlign
messages:
From: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@medalign.de>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: itsec@medalign.de
Date: 2028-06-15T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery call — On‑prem options

Thanks for the intro call earlier today. Good to meet both of you. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned on constraints and what we'll need from Redwood before procurement can move forward:

- Regulatory & residency: all patient data (PHI) must remain in the EU; preferred Frankfurt region.
- Air‑gap requirements: for the model inference path on certain workloads we require an isolated environment with no outbound internet egress. Staged connectivity for updates only (manual/approved channels).
- Network constraints: strict outbound port restrictions (we will share an approved ports list), no direct public IPs for inference nodes, traffic must traverse our on‑prem firewall and a dedicated DMZ.
- KMS/HSM: keys must be customer‑owned; Redwood must support a customer KMS or HSM integration (bring‑your‑own).
- Audit & evidence: SOC2 + port‑level evidence and recent penetration test summary required for our infosec review.

Next asks from MedAlign: can you (1) confirm which Redwood components must be reachable from our network vs which can be fully hosted in customer VPC/on‑prem, (2) provide a short procurement one‑pager that outlines hosting options + rough pricing bands and SOW bullets, and (3) share a network diagram + ports checklist we can give to our NetOps team.

Thanks — happy to set a follow up with our NetOps next week.

— Anna Schmidt
Director, IT & Compliance
MedAlign GmbH


From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@medalign.de>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-15T21:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery call — On‑prem options

Anna — thanks for the clear summary and for surfacing the requirements. Below is our concise recap (so your stakeholders can forward internally) plus proposed immediate next steps and owners. We've attached a stub network sketch and a ports checklist for your NetOps team; we'll iterate once they provide their allowed list.

Recap (what we heard)
• Data residency: Frankfurt (eu‑central) required for stored data and inference.
• Air‑gapped inference for selected workloads: no internet egress; updates via approved channel only.
• Key management: customer KMS/HSM required; Redwood must support Bring‑Your‑Own‑KMS and offline key injection for on‑prem enclaves.
• Connectivity: no public IPs on inference nodes; connections originate from customer network to Redwood where absolutely necessary (PrivateLink/Direct Connect model preferred).
• Evidence: SOC2 reports + port/test evidence needed for procurement.

What runs where (high level)
• Control plane (account management, billing, UI): hosted in Redwood region but can be configured to use private connectivity (VPC peering or PrivateLink).
• Model runtime / inference engines: can be deployed in customer VPC or on‑prem dedicated enclave depending on procurement. For full air‑gap, runtime lives fully in your environment with only manual sync channels for model updates.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
1) Send NetOps‑ready network diagram + ports checklist (attachment v1) — owner: Soojin Lee (we did this); ask: confirm allowed ports by 2028‑06‑19.
2) Technical deep dive + NetOps sync (30–45m) — owner: Jonas Weber (solutions) — target week of 2028‑06‑22.
3) Procurement one‑pager (hosting options, model sizing bands, SOW bullets) — owner: Soojin Lee — draft by 2028‑06‑18.
4) Provide SOC2 + attestation excerpts and recent pen‑test summary — owner: Redwood Security — ETA 2028‑06‑20.

Questions for MedAlign
• Can you confirm a single point of contact for NetOps and for procurement (name + email)?
• Do you have an internal timeline for go/no‑go on PoC (we'll align PoC scope once NetOps constraints are confirmed)?

Attachments: medalign-network-sketch.pdf (stub), medalign-compliance-sheet.xlsx (template)

I'll follow up with the procurement one‑pager first thing tomorrow. Thanks again — we appreciate the thoroughness.

— Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0123

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@medalign.de>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-16T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery call — On‑prem options

Anna / Soojin — quick technical clarifications following Soojin's recap so NetOps has actionable details before the sync: 

1) Network pattern we recommend for air‑gapped workloads:
   - Option A (preferred for max isolation): inference nodes deployed inside MedAlign on‑prem or customer‑VPC with no outbound internet access. Model artifacts are updated via signed offline bundles pushed through a controlled upload gateway we stand up in your DMZ (pull only with signed manifests).
   - Option B (hybrid): inference in customer VPC with a PrivateLink to Redwood control plane; telemetry buffered and forwarded only to endpoints you permit.

2) Ports & protocols (starter list) — we'll finalize after your NetOps shares their allowed list:
   - 443 (HTTPS) outbound from control plane to customer PrivateLink endpoint — only for management, optional.
   - 22 (SSH) — only for troubleshooting on scheduled windows, not for routine traffic.
   - Custom telemetry ports — optional and can be tunneled through PrivateLink.

3) KMS/HSM integration:
   - We support customer‑managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with on‑prem HSM for key wrapping. For air‑gapped enclaves we support manual key injection workflows and can produce audit logs for every key operation.

4) PoC proposal (30 days):
   - Phase 1: NetOps sync + test connectivity (week 1).
   - Phase 2: Deploy a small inference pool (1–2 GPUs) in a customer VPC or on‑prem VM; run synthetic traffic to validate latency and egress constraints (weeks 2–3).
   - Phase 3: Run sample production traffic and collect audit logs for your compliance team (week 4).

Please let me know the NetOps contact and preferred windows for a 45m session next week. I'll bring a checklist and a minimal test plan.

— Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
